paper_title: PELMS Pre-training for Effective Low-Shot Multi-Document Summarization
caption: Low-shot pre-trained model performance on the multi-document summarization (MDS) task with ROUGE-G scores (geometric mean of ROUGE-1/2/L) aggregated over 6 MDS benchmarks. We compare with fully-supervised training (solid lines) and with adapter training (dashed lines) where only 5% of model parameters are tuned. achieves stronger overall performance at all data quantities and training methods when compared to competitive long-input summarization models.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the performance of various models on a multi-document summarization task, measured by the ROUGE-G score, across different numbers of training examples. The x-axis represents the number of training examples on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 4 to 64. The y-axis represents the overall ROUGE-G score on a linear scale, ranging from 11.0 to 19.0, with tick labels at intervals of 2.0. The plot shows seven lines representing different models and training methods: PELMS (green solid line with circle markers), PELMS (5%) (green dashed line with circle markers), Primera (red solid line with square markers), Primera (5%) (red dashed line with square markers), Pegasus-X (blue solid line with triangle markers), Pegasus-X (5%) (blue dashed line with triangle markers), Centrum (yellow solid line with diamond markers), and Centum (5%) (yellow dashed line with diamond markers). Starting at 4 training examples, PELMS begins at approximately 17.0 and increases to 19.0 at 64 training examples; PELMS (5%) begins at approximately 16.0 and increases to 18.5; Primera begins at approximately 15.0 and increases to 17.5; Primera (5%) begins at approximately 15.0 and increases to 16.5; Pegasus-X begins at approximately 12.0 and increases to 14.5; Pegasus-X (5%) begins at approximately 13.0 and remains relatively stable around 14.5; Centrum begins at approximately 14.5 and increases to 16.0; Centum (5%) begins at approximately 14.0 and increases to 15.5.
